subject: Pilot runway smoothing and tiered offer for Claritone Labs
messages:
From: Ben Harper <ben.harper@claritone.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot — quick ask on extension and smoothing

Evelyn,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team is bullish and we want to stretch the pilot a bit to get the last integration pieces in. Two asks from engineering + procurement: 1) can we get an extra three weeks on the time-box (same scope) and 2) can you propose a smoothing option so we don't spike our bill if we run a concentrated test next month?

We're not looking for a large discount, more of a predictable cost path and a small buffer for burst runs. Procurement (procurement@claritone.com) asked that any extension be simple (one-line amendment) rather than a long addendum.

Ben
Ben Harper
Head of ML Platforms | Claritone Labs
ben.harper@claritone.com

P.S. happy to hop on a 15-min call if that helps. Attachment: proposed timeline (we'll send separately).

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Ben Harper <ben.harper@claritone.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot — quick ask on extension and smoothing

Ben — thanks, really glad to hear the team is seeing value. We can do a short extension plus a cost-smoothing option. Two quick approaches that would be simple and align with procurement's preference for minimal paperwork: 

Option A — Timebox extension + graduated discount
- Add 3 weeks to current pilot end-date (no change to scope)
- Graduated overage discount: 10% off overage for first 20% above expected burn, 20% off for next 10% (caps at 30% above expected)
- One-line amendment referencing the existing SOW and new end date (legal-friendly).

Option B — Burst credit bucket (prepaid)
- Add a 200k-token burst bucket that can be consumed during the pilot; unused portion converts to credit against early invoices
- No change to end date required; invoice shows separate line-item for burst credit

I attached a short PDF that lays this out with numbers and a sample invoice line (Claritone_Pilot_TieredOffer_20260706.pdf). From a commercial standpoint, A is lower friction for finance; B gives you budgeting certainty for spikes.

If procurement prefers the one-line amendment route, we can draft it and circulate for signature — I will loop in Karthik for any price concessions and Marissa on billing. Happy to jump on a 15-minute call this afternoon.

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Looping you both in — Ben asked for a 3-week timebox extension and a smoothing option. I sketched two options (A = timebox + graduated overage discount; B = prepaid burst bucket that converts unused to credit). PDF attached. Procurement asked for a one-line amendment if possible.

Quick asks: 
- Karthik: can we support the graduated discount in Option A? If so, any recommended caps or guardrails we should call out? Legal prefers minimal language in the amendment per Ben's procurement note.
- Marissa: if customer picks B (burst bucket), what does accounting need for the invoice line? Will we credit unused portion automatically or do you need a journal?

I propose we offer Option A as the default and Option B as an alternate if they need strict budgeting. Thoughts?

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot — quick ask on extension and smoothing

Evelyn — thanks for the context and clear options. My read: offer Option A as the primary path but sweeten it slightly to make conversion easier. Suggested concession:

- Keep the 3-week extension.
- Improve the graduated overage tiers to: 12% off overage for first 25% above forecast, 22% off for the next 10% (cap at 35% above forecast).
- If they sign the amendment within 5 business days we'll include a one-time onboarding credit equal to the cost of a 50k-token burst (applied if they convert to a committed package within 60 days).

Finance/legal notes: 
- Marissa: billing can do the prepaid bucket credit conversion as a contra-invoice item; we just need the PO number and a short description.
- Legal prefers a single-sentence amendment that references the existing SOW and adjusts the end date / billing line; they don't want to reopen other commercial terms (good).

I think this is a low-cost concession with strong conversion signal. Approve and I can sign off client-side when procurement sends PO.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Commercial Finance | Redwood Inference
